in_greek.name: Καρμεσία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καρμεσία προέρχεται από τη λέξη 'Καρμήλος', που σημαίνει κήπος ή τόπος πνευματικότητας. Είναι συνδεδεμένο με τον Θεό και τον πνευματικό κόσμο, και εκπέμπει αίσθηση γαλήνης και ηρεμίας. Το όνομα χρησιμοποιείται στην χριστιανική παράδοση και η σημασία του είναι βαθιά και σύνθετη.

historical_references.reference: In the 11th century, there was a hermit named Carinus who lived in a cave near the town of Montalbano in Italy. He was known for his devotion to the Blessed Virgin Mary and was called 'Carmelite' due to the mountainous location of his hermitage which was compared to the biblical Mount Carmel. Over time, the name 'Carmelite' evolved into 'Carmessian'.

The Carmessian Order was officially recognized by Pope John XXII in 1328. It was a branch of the Carmelites, specifically focused on living in communities as opposed to as hermits. The name 'Carmessian' became associated with this order, distinguishing it from the other branches of the Carmelites.
